To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the joint in- and out- degree distribution of a preferential attachment network is regularly varying; (ii) the joint in-degree and size distribution of a preferational attachment network is not regularly varying.

(1) the joint mass function associated with the preferential attachment process is regularly varying; (2) the mass function of the out-degrees of a preferential attachment process can be embedded into a regularly varying density function; (3) the mass function associated with in- and out-degrees can be embedded into the product of two regularly varying density functions.
